quest.guildmark.story.lair.spider_den.0: Webs over the old mine mouth, thick as sailcloth. Something big spins them.
quest.guildmark.story.lair.spider_den.1: The goats wander into the hills and come back as husks of skin.
quest.guildmark.story.lair.spider_den.2: A hunter came back babbling about eyes. Lots of eyes.
quest.guildmark.story.lair.old_mine.0: The old mine was sealed after the cave-in. The lamps are lit down there again.
quest.guildmark.story.lair.old_mine.1: We hear picks in the deep seam at night. Nobody's been paid to dig there in forty years.
quest.guildmark.story.lair.old_mine.2: The foreman died in the collapse, they say. Then who keeps buying lamp oil?
quest.guildmark.story.lair.bandit_camp.0: WANTED, dead or alive: the chief of the camp in the hills. Reward on proof.
quest.guildmark.story.lair.bandit_camp.1: They took the tax cart and the man driving it. We know where they sleep.
quest.guildmark.story.lair.bandit_camp.2: Smoke from a camp where no camp should be. Their chief has a price on his head.
quest.guildmark.story.lair.barrow.0: The old barrow on the ridge has opened. The dead want their things back.
quest.guildmark.story.lair.barrow.1: Grave goods are turning up in the market. Somebody, or something, is digging.
quest.guildmark.story.lair.barrow.2: Bells ring under the hill at night. There are no bells under the hill.
A crone in the hollow sells cures that turn people green. Close her shop.
Three children followed a light into the woods. Two came back.
The well water smells of mushrooms, and the frogs have started talking.
quest.guildmark.story.lair.ashen_pit.0: The ground split open beyond the river and it's still burning.
quest.guildmark.story.lair.ashen_pit.1: Black-boned things climb out of the ash at night. The forest is half gone.
quest.guildmark.story.lair.ashen_pit.2: Something down in the pit is keeping the fire fed. Put it out.
message.guildmark.coach.ride_hover: Ride to %s for %s Guild Marks. Your following guild members come too, and nearby party members can ride after you.
message.guildmark.coach.none: No coach stops here. Coaches run along finished Trade Roads, from villages that have one.
message.guildmark.coach.gone: No coach from here goes there.
message.guildmark.coach.escort: Your charge won't ride a coach. Walk them there.
message.guildmark.coach.arrived: The coach rattles down the Trade Road and sets you down at %s.
message.guildmark.title.none: You haven't earned any titles yet. Milestones in the Guildmark advancement tab grant them.
message.guildmark.title.cleared: You're known by your name alone.
character.guildmark.pip.epithet: Wandering bard, collector of other people's glory
character.guildmark.pip.intro: Ah! An adventurer! An actual one, with dents! I'm Pip Larkspur, bard of the high roads, and I've sung the same three songs for a year. I need new material. You need someone to make you famous. We're perfect for each other.
character.guildmark.pip.step0: First, the small matter of my lute. Some brute sat on it and every string snapped. A dozen strings, please. Spider silk if you can, they're the only ones that hold a tune.
character.guildmark.pip.step0.note: "String, not twine. Twine is for parcels. Music deserves better."
character.guildmark.pip.step1: Now, a ballad needs a monster. Something green, silent and horribly sudden. Go and blow up, ah, no, stop half a dozen creepers, and remember what it felt like. I'll need details.
character.guildmark.pip.step1.note: "Rhymes with creeper: keeper, sleeper, reaper. Make it a reaper."
character.guildmark.pip.step2: Every great ballad ends in a barrow. There's a dead lord in one out past the hills, and no one's ever written a verse about him that wasn't a lament. Give me a triumph instead.
character.guildmark.pip.step2.note: "Try not to die. Tragic endings sell, but I'd miss you."
character.guildmark.pip.waiting: The song can't finish itself! Off you go, and do something worth rhyming.
character.guildmark.pip.finale: There it is. Strings, a monster, and a barrow. That's a ballad! Here, I wrote it all down, every deed you've done. I'll sing it in every tavern from here to the coast. Come back when you've done something new and I'll write you another verse.
character.guildmark.pip.done: Back for another verse? Do something worth singing about, and I'll be here.
character.guildmark.pip.gift.lore: As sung by Pip Larkspur, in every tavern that would have him
character.guildmark.pip.topic.songs.0: Three! The one about the miller's daughter, the one about the other miller's daughter, and the one about the goat.
character.guildmark.pip.topic.songs.1: The goat one is my finest work. Audiences disagree, loudly, and sometimes with vegetables. Which is why I need you.
character.guildmark.pip.topic.fame: Why would I want to be famous?
character.guildmark.pip.topic.fame.0: Here's how fame works. You do something brave. I make it rhyme. A hundred taverns sing it, and in ten years nobody remembers what really happened, only the song.
character.guildmark.pip.topic.fame.1: So you do the brave part, and leave the truth to me. Everybody wins. Especially me.
character.guildmark.pip.ballad.intro:
THE BALLAD OF %s

As sung by Pip Larkspur, bard of the high roads, to whoever would listen and several who wouldn't.
character.guildmark.pip.ballad.outro:
And still the road goes on, and still %s walks it.

The song's not over. Pip is taking notes.
character.guildmark.pip.verse.none: There once was an adventurer called %s, who hadn't done anything yet. Lovely boots, though!
character.guildmark.pip.verse.paid: %s took a note from a village board, and the job was done by dusk. A small beginning, but every legend starts with one.
character.guildmark.pip.verse.advance_bu: When %s's coin built the village lamps, the lanes grew bright, and nobody tripped over the chickens ever again.
character.guildmark.pip.verse.champion: A champion stalked the hills, named and proud, until %s cut the name short.
character.guildmark.pip.verse.trade_road: %s paved the way from town to town, and now the carts roll and the merchants grumble less.
character.guildmark.pip.verse.lair: Down in the den where the dark things breed, %s walked in alone and walked out with the master's head.
character.guildmark.pip.verse.first_shar: Wren found a shard of a crown long broken, and %s said: then let's find the rest.
character.guildmark.pip.verse.guild_foun: %s set a name in the guild's great book, and a banner flew that hadn't flown before.
character.guildmark.pip.verse.banner: Over the bell of a grateful town, %s raised a banner, and the village sang beneath it.
character.guildmark.pip.verse.siege: The horde came howling under a moonless sky. %s stood at the bell, and the bell still rings.
character.guildmark.pip.verse.repelled: A rival guild came knocking with a captain and a claim. %s answered at the bell, and the captain went home lighter.
character.guildmark.pip.verse.legendary: From a sealed cache came a blade of legend, and it chose %s. Smart blade.
character.guildmark.pip.verse.city: A hamlet once, a city now, with a keep of stone, built note by note by %s.
character.guildmark.pip.verse.takeover: %s challenged a rival's captain for a town, and won it fair, with the whole town watching.
character.guildmark.pip.verse.seven_shar: Seven shards of the Hollow Crown, seven courtiers fallen, and %s holding the lot.
character.guildmark.pip.verse.hollow_kin: The Hollow King sat on a throne of nothing, until %s came and broke the crown. Sing it loud, sing it long: the Wardens live again.
character.guildmark.idris.epithet: Magister of the Starwatch, keeper of the old sorceries
character.guildmark.idris.intro: Mind the lecterns, they're older than the city. I am Idris Vael, Magister of the Starwatch. We read the sky, we keep the old sorceries, and lately we've been reading things in the sky I would rather not.
character.guildmark.idris.step0: If you'd study with us, show me you can bend the weave. I've loosed five ward-lights over the plaza. Put them out, and with sorcery, mind. A blade passes straight through them.
character.guildmark.idris.step0.note: "No staff? Take one of ours. Point the crystal at the light, not at the Magister."
character.guildmark.idris.step1: Clean work. Welcome to the Starwatch, Candle. Now, our star charts are written in ink ground from lapis, and the last of ours went into a very long footnote. Two dozen pieces, if you would.
character.guildmark.idris.step1.note: "Lapis lazuli. Not blue rocks. I have been brought blue rocks."
character.guildmark.idris.step2: The phantoms have taken to circling the city by night, and you cannot chart a sky that keeps flapping. Bring down half a dozen, Lamp, and we can see again.
character.guildmark.idris.step2.note: "They come for those who haven't slept. For once, staying up late is a virtue."
character.guildmark.idris.step3: A hedge-witch has our star-glass, the lens we read the omens through. She took it from a careless Lamp and fled to a hollow in the wilds. Fetch it back, Lantern. She has had time to prepare.
character.guildmark.idris.step3.note: "Don't look through the glass. Whatever she has put in it, I would rather see it first."
character.guildmark.idris.step4: Through the glass I've seen who sent her. Silvan Marrow. He was a Beacon of this order before he learned to read the forbidden chart, the one that shows where the stars go out. He waits at the old observatory. End it, Beacon. Gently, if he lets you.
character.guildmark.idris.step4.note: "He was my best student. Don't let him talk. He was always better at talking."
character.guildmark.idris.waiting: The stars will wait. I, unfortunately, am less patient. Off you go.
character.guildmark.idris.finale: The chart. And Silvan... no, don't tell me. The Starwatch names you a Star, the first in thirty years. This staff was made for the last one. It has sat on a shelf waiting for someone who earned it.
character.guildmark.idris.done: Back again? Look up tonight, Star, and tell me what you see.
character.guildmark.idris.gated: Not yet. That work wants someone the guilds rate at least %s. I'll not send a Candle where a Beacon might not come back.
character.guildmark.idris.work: There is always work in a library. Have a look at this.
character.guildmark.idris.woken: Mm? Ah. The stars keep late hours, and so, it seems, do you.
character.guildmark.idris.topic.starwatc: We watch. Every night for four hundred years, a Star or a Beacon has sat at the top of this city and written down the sky. The sorceries came later. You learn a great deal about light, looking at it that long.
These days we teach whoever has the patience. The patience is rarer than the gift.
character.guildmark.idris.topic.omens: What have you seen in the sky?
character.guildmark.idris.topic.omens.0: Stars going out. Not falling, not fading: going out, one by one, in the north, where the old King's throne stands empty.
character.guildmark.idris.topic.omens.1: Something is drinking the light. When I find out what, I would very much like to be wrong.
character.guildmark.corra.intro: You've the look of someone who holds a sword the right way round. I'm Corra Wystan, Knight-Commander of the Hearthsworn. We keep the Wardfires lit and the dead off the roads. The Order always needs hands, but it doesn't take them on faith.
character.guildmark.corra.step0: Step into a ring with one of my knights. A spar, nothing more: the first to give ground yields. Show me you can take a blow and give one back.
character.guildmark.corra.step0.note: "They'll go easy on you. Don't you dare go easy on them."
character.guildmark.corra.step1: You held. Kneel... and rise, Squire of the Hearthsworn. Your first duty is the oldest one. Hollow soldiers walk the roads out of this city. Put ten of them back in the ground.
character.guildmark.corra.step1.note: "They were soldiers once. Give them a soldier's end."
character.guildmark.corra.step2: There's a Wardfire on the road out of the city that the Hollow have gone for three nights running. Tonight it's yours. Hold it till dawn, Sworn. If it goes out, a whole road goes dark.
character.guildmark.corra.step2.note: "Two of mine will stand with you. Keep the fire at your back and the dead in front."
character.guildmark.corra.step3: A thieves' ring that calls itself the Quiet Hand meets somewhere in this city, under our noses. The Widow who runs it keeps a ledger of every guard she has ever bought. Bring me that ledger, Knight.
character.guildmark.corra.step3.note: "Don't kill anyone. A thief in a cell can talk. A thief in the ground can't."
character.guildmark.corra.step4: The Order has hunted the Dusk Rider for a hundred years. Every Banneret before you rode out to meet it, and every one came back on a shield. I wouldn't ask if I thought anyone else could do it. Bring the Rider down.
character.guildmark.corra.step4.note: "It comes with the dusk. Meet it on open ground, and don't let it run you down."
character.guildmark.corra.waiting: The dead don't rest because we do. On your way, and come back with it done.
character.guildmark.corra.finale: It's over. A hundred years, and it's over. You've earned a title no one has held since my mother's day: Hearthwarden. And this. Hearthbrand was forged in the first Wardfire. It burns for those who keep the oath.
character.guildmark.corra.done: Hearthwarden. The fires burn a little brighter with you on the road.
character.guildmark.corra.gated: Not yet. That's a task for someone the guilds rate %s or better. I'll not bury a squire to prove a point.
character.guildmark.corra.work: There's always a road that needs clearing. Here.
character.guildmark.corra.woken: Hm? I'm awake. I'm always awake. What is it?
character.guildmark.corra.rival: One more thing. Word is you've been seen with the Widow's people. I'll not ask. But bring me that ledger and they'll know who did it, and they'll never have you back.
character.guildmark.corra.expelled: You stole the Ember from this house. Get out of my sight. The Hearthsworn have nothing for you, now or ever.
character.guildmark.corra.topic.oath.0: Keep the fire. Keep the road. Keep faith with those who sleep. Three lines, and we spend our lives learning them.
character.guildmark.corra.topic.oath.1: Most knights swear to a lord. We swear to a campfire. People laugh, until it's the only light for twenty miles.
No. The Wardens were something else: road-walkers, no home, no lord. When they fell, the Order took up what it could. Their fires. Their roads. Not their name. We hadn't earned it.
If you ever meet one, a real one, I'd give a great deal to shake their hand.
character.guildmark.odile.epithet: The Widow, who runs the Quiet Hand
character.guildmark.odile.intro: Close the hatch, dear, there's a draught. You'll have heard of me, or you wouldn't have climbed all those stairs. Odile Fenn. Some call me the Widow, though I've never married. It discourages suitors. We are the Quiet Hand, and we only take from those who will never miss it.
character.guildmark.odile.step0: Light fingers first, then we talk. Lift three purses off the nobles walking this city, and don't let them see you do it. Come at them from behind, crouch low, and be quick about it.
character.guildmark.odile.step0.note: "If they turn round, walk away. Never run. Running is a confession."
character.guildmark.odile.step1: Not bad at all. Welcome to the Hand, Lookout. Now, House Varn keeps a ledger of debts in their manor in the noble quarter, and a great many people would sleep easier if it went missing. Walk in, take it, walk out. Their guards are poorly paid and bored. Don't let them stop being bored.
character.guildmark.odile.step1.note: "Keep to the shadows and keep low. Bright rooms and loud boots are how people hang."
character.guildmark.odile.step2: Some cutthroat crew is robbing caravans on the roads out of the city, and they're not ours. Robbing travellers is bad for business, Cutpurse. Our business. Thin them out.
character.guildmark.odile.step2.note: "Eight should send the message. They're not clever, but they can count."
character.guildmark.odile.step3: Now a real job. The Hearthsworn keep a relic in their chapter house, the Ember of the First Hearth, in a little gold box. I have a buyer who'll pay more for that box than the knights earn in a lifetime. Knights are sharper than house guards, Picklock. Mind them.
character.guildmark.odile.step3.note: "Knights look up as well as down. Keep to the corners."
character.guildmark.odile.step4: This is the one I've waited thirty years for. The Regent keeps the Crown's own seal in the palace vault. With it I can write any order in the city. Bring me the seal, Shadow, and you'll never need to steal again. Not that you'll stop.
character.guildmark.odile.step4.note: "The vault guards are not bored. Patience is the only tool you need."
character.guildmark.odile.waiting: Still here? A job doesn't do itself, dear. Not even ours.
character.guildmark.odile.finale: The Regent's seal. Oh, that is beautiful. You've done what I never could, my dear. The Hand has had a Right Hand only once before, and she's the reason I wear black. This was hers. Widow's Kiss. Use it kindly.
character.guildmark.odile.done: My Right Hand. Sit, have a drink. Steal something on your way out, it keeps you in practice.
character.guildmark.odile.gated: Patience, dear. That job wants someone the guilds rate %s at least, and I don't send children into palaces.
character.guildmark.odile.work: Always something for clever hands. Here.
character.guildmark.odile.woken: Mm, at this hour? You're either very brave or very drunk. Sit.
character.guildmark.odile.rival: You wear the knights' colours, don't you? Under the coat, where you think no one sees. Take this job and they'll know it was you. The Order doesn't forgive. Neither do I, as it happens. I just smile more.
character.guildmark.odile.expelled: You brought the knights my ledger. Do you know how many people that ledger was keeping safe? Go. And don't ever climb these stairs again.
character.guildmark.odile.topic.hand.0: A family, of sorts. Cutpurses, picklocks, a forger, two very good liars. Every city has a thieves' ring. This city has a polite one.
character.guildmark.odile.topic.hand.1: We have rules. Nobody who can't spare it. Nobody hurt who doesn't deserve it. And nobody, ever, talks to the knights.
character.guildmark.odile.topic.widow: Why do they call you the Widow?
character.guildmark.odile.topic.widow.0: Black is a practical colour. It doesn't show dirt, it doesn't show blood, and men stop asking you to dance.
character.guildmark.odile.topic.widow.1: And I did lose someone, once. The best thief this city ever had. She stole the moon off the bottom of a well, or so she told it. I keep her knife. One day I will give it away.
character.guildmark.bram.meet: Evening. They say you pay on time. Mind if I share your fire?
character.guildmark.bram.intro: Bram Hale, late of the Greyhart Company. Late being the word that matters. I've a good sword arm, a bad knee and no master, and you look like someone who could use the first and put up with the second. Honest work for honest pay, and I'll walk with you.
character.guildmark.bram.join: Aye, done. Lead on. I'll watch your back, you watch the pay.
character.guildmark.bram.decline: Fair enough. I've sat by worse fires. Come and find me when you want a sword.
character.guildmark.bram.hello.1: Go on. I'm listening. It's not as if I've anywhere better to be.
character.guildmark.bram.follow: Aye. I'll walk where I can see your back.
character.guildmark.bram.wait: I'll hold here. Don't be long. Standing still makes my knee talk.
character.guildmark.bram.part: As you like. I'll wait here, I'm not hard to find. Big man, bad mood. Come back if you need a sword.
character.guildmark.bram.rejoin: Thought you might. Same terms as before, and the same knee. Let's walk.
character.guildmark.bram.step0: There are raiders on these roads, and I know whose colours they ride under. Harl Voss, my old captain. Put down eight of his riders and I'll tell you what he did to earn it. I don't ask favours often, so take it as meant.
character.guildmark.bram.step0.note: Bram wants the raiders who ride with Harl Voss thinned out: eight of them.
character.guildmark.bram.step1: Those riders have a camp, and it's Harl's. Walls, watchfires, the whole proud mess, and the Greyhart pay chest in there somewhere, if he hasn't drunk it dry. Clear it out, and stand beside me when I face him. I'll owe you more for that than for all the rest.
character.guildmark.bram.step1.note: Bram wants Harl Voss's bandit camp cleared, and Harl with it.
character.guildmark.bram.step2: Harl's dead, and I find I'm not glad, which surprises me. One debt left. Where the Greyharts fell there's a Hill Troll camp now, and our colours hang in it like washing. Bring a troll down, and bring the colours home.
character.guildmark.bram.step2.note: Bram wants a Hill Troll brought down, so the Greyhart colours can come home from its camp.
character.guildmark.bram.waiting: Not done yet? I've waited longer for worse. Take your time, but not all of it.
character.guildmark.bram.step0.done: Eight. Good. I said I'd tell you what he'd done. He led the Greyharts into a troll valley and rode off with the pay chest while we were busy dying. Sixty good men.
character.guildmark.bram.step1.done: It's done. He knew me at the end. Looked right at me and said my name like it was a joke. I'd hoped it would feel like more than this.
character.guildmark.bram.gated: Not yet. Ask me again when we've shared a few more fires.
character.guildmark.bram.finale: The colours, home at last. Take this, with my thanks. It was Harl's sword once, and I had the smith hammer the lie out of it and put the hart on the blade where it belongs. There's one Greyhart left, and he stands where you stand.
character.guildmark.bram.done: Shield-brother. Where to, and who's paying?
character.guildmark.bram.standing.0: Cold. You've done nothing to earn my trust, and a thing or two to lose it. Mind you, pay is still pay.
character.guildmark.bram.standing.1: Wary. Not bad, not good. I've worked for worse, and I've watched them hang.
character.guildmark.bram.standing.2: Better than it was. You pay what you say, and you don't flinch. That's two more than most.
character.guildmark.bram.standing.3: I'd stand at your shoulder in a bad spot, and I don't say that to many. Don't make a liar of me.
character.guildmark.bram.standing.4: Near enough sworn, if you want it said. I'd walk into a troll's kitchen for you, and I've done worse for less.
character.guildmark.bram.standing.5: Sworn. Shield-brothers, you and I. The Greyharts would have had you, and that's the best thing I know how to say.
character.guildmark.bram.gift: Now that's a gift a man can use. Thank you. I'll not make a speech of it.
character.guildmark.bram.gift_again: You've fed me once already today. Any more and I'll get ideas, or fat.
character.guildmark.bram.topic.greyharts: Sixty swords and a grey hart on the banner. We took honest contracts, kept to them, and never left a village worse than we found it. That was the whole creed, and a decent one.
It ended in a valley, under a captain I'd have followed anywhere. That's the trouble with that kind of captain. Ask me about him when I've had a drink.
character.guildmark.bram.topic.coin: Why does coin matter so much to you?
character.guildmark.bram.topic.coin.0: Because a Guild Mark in the hand is the only promise I've ever seen kept. I've been paid in thanks, in glory and in fine speeches, and I've never once eaten a speech.
character.guildmark.bram.topic.coin.1: A contract's the same. Two names, a price, a day it's done. Break one with me and we're finished. Keep it, and I'd walk through a wall for you. It's simple, which is why I like it.
character.guildmark.bram.leave: I've been sold out once, and I'll not stand and watch it happen twice. I'm done. Keep your road.
character.guildmark.bram.cold: Not today. Give me time to cool, and a drink to help.
character.guildmark.bram.return: I thought it over, with a tankard's help. You're not good company yet, but I've had worse. Lead on.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.approve.fi: Ha. Now that was a proper fight.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.approve.he: Honest work, honestly done. I like that.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.disapprove: Thieving from honest folk? I'd hoped you were better than that.
You killed someone who couldn't fight back. I'll not forget it.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.faction.he: The Hearthsworn. They keep the fires lit. Well chosen.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.faction.qu: The Quiet Hand. Thieves with manners are still thieves.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.ask: A word, when you've a moment. I've a favour to ask.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.camp.0: First contract I ever took with the Greyharts was a wedding. Sixty swords to guard one bride, and the groom's mother sent the lot of us to the kitchen for being underfoot. Best fed we ever were.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.camp.1: I joined at nineteen. Harl Voss was captain then, a laughing man who knew every recruit's name by supper. I'd have followed him off a cliff. Seems I did.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.camp.2: Sixty of us stood in that valley, and fifty-nine had the decency to die. I lay under the colours and the trolls took me for dead, and I let them. I've never forgiven myself for being good at it.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.region: New country. Don't trust it yet.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.capital: Fine walls. I'd wager the prices are finer. Mind your purse.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.night: Light's going. Time we found a fire.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.rain: Rain. My knee told me an hour ago.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.deep: Too much rock over my head. I don't like it.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.hurt: You're bleeding badly. Fall back and drink something. Now.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.boss: That's a big one. Good. Big ones fall loudest.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.victory: Still standing. That counts as a win.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.downed: Down, but not out. Give me a moment.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.revived: Obliged. Don't tell anyone I needed it.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.respawn: Back from the dead. Try not to make a habit of it.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.idle.0: I've slept in worse places than this. Not many, mind.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.idle.1: No decent pint in a week. I'm not complaining. I'm noting it.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.idle.2: A man who says money isn't everything has always got some.
character.guildmark.bram.bark.swap: Someone else, is it? Fine. I'll wait here until their sword breaks.
character.guildmark.ysolde.meet: Oh, a lit Wardfire. Light keep you, friend. May I sit with you?
character.guildmark.ysolde.intro: Ysolde Marsh, pilgrim of the Lamplighters. We kept the Wardfires lit along the roads, once. I pray, I heal, and I trip over my own hem, though I am much better at the first two. If you'll have a pilgrim for company, I would be glad to walk with you.
character.guildmark.ysolde.join: Oh, thank you, friend. Truly. Lead on, and I will try not to trip over anything important.
character.guildmark.ysolde.decline: Of course. I'll sit with this fire a while, it deserves the company. Come and find me when you're ready.
character.guildmark.ysolde.hello.0: Hello, friend. Is something the matter, or are we only being sociable? I do like sociable.
character.guildmark.ysolde.hello.1: Mm? I was saying a prayer for the road. It will keep. What is it?
character.guildmark.ysolde.follow: Of course. Right behind you, and only occasionally on the ground.
character.guildmark.ysolde.wait: I'll keep the place for you. Don't be long, and light keep you.
character.guildmark.ysolde.part: Then I'll wait here, and keep a candle lit for you. Come and find me if you need me. Light keep you.
character.guildmark.ysolde.rejoin: Oh, I'm so glad you came back. My last candle was nearly out. Shall we?
character.guildmark.ysolde.step0: The roads my order kept are not safe anymore. Hollow soldiers walk them, and they should be lying down. Help me put eight of them to rest, and I'll say the words over each one, if you'll give me a moment. They were somebody's sons once.
character.guildmark.ysolde.step0.note: Ysolde wants eight Hollow soldiers put to rest on the roads her order once kept.
character.guildmark.ysolde.step1: That was our whole work, you know. Keeping the fires lit, so no one walks the dark alone. There are three Wardfires out there gone cold. Kindle them with me, any you haven't lit yet, and the order will feel a little less dead.
character.guildmark.ysolde.step1.note: Ysolde wants three cold Wardfires kindled, any you have not lit yet.
character.guildmark.ysolde.step2: The Lamplighters once served the Wardens, and carried their lamps down the roads. There is a Warden's Watch where the Fallen Warden still keeps his post, and he is not at peace. I would go down to him, but not alone. Will you help me give him rest?
character.guildmark.ysolde.step2.note: Ysolde wants the Fallen Warden given rest, down in his Warden's Watch.
character.guildmark.ysolde.waiting: Take the time you need, friend. But not too much, if you can. The dead aren't resting.
character.guildmark.ysolde.step0.done: Eight at rest. Thank you, friend. I said the words over every one, and I think the roads breathe easier. So do I.
character.guildmark.ysolde.step1.done: Three fires, burning again. Can you see them from here? That is what we were for. Thank you for helping me remember.
character.guildmark.ysolde.gated: Not yet, friend. Ask me again when we have walked a little further together.
character.guildmark.ysolde.finale: He is at rest. I felt it go quiet, like a bell that has finished ringing. Take the censer, friend, its flame has not gone out since the order began, and I would rather it burned in your hands than sat in mine. I am sworn to you now. Whatever falls on you, I will be there with the light.
character.guildmark.ysolde.done: Light keep you, friend. Where shall we walk today?
character.guildmark.ysolde.standing.0: Like strangers at a fire that hasn't caught. It may yet. I would like it to.
character.guildmark.ysolde.standing.1: Carefully, I think. I'm still deciding about you, and you about me. That's allowed.
character.guildmark.ysolde.standing.2: Better. The fire has caught, and I'm glad of your company, whatever else is true.
character.guildmark.ysolde.standing.3: I trust you, friend. I would put my life in your hands and my prayers at your back, and I do not say that lightly.
character.guildmark.ysolde.standing.4: Close as kin, nearly. A step or two more and I'll call you sworn, and mean it.
character.guildmark.ysolde.standing.5: Sworn. By light, by road, and by every fire we've kindled. There is nothing between us now but the road.
character.guildmark.ysolde.gift: Oh, how kind. Thank you, friend. You've made a pilgrim's whole day.
character.guildmark.ysolde.gift_again: You're too good to me, but you gave me one today already. Keep it for tomorrow, and light keep you for the thought.
character.guildmark.ysolde.topic.lamplig: A small order, never more than a score of us along all the roads. Every Wardfire had one of us to tend it. Trim the wick, say the words, keep the dark honest. Nobody sang about us. We kept the lights on.
The Hearthsworn keep the fires now, and they keep them well. I am not bitter. Only a little, on the mornings I forget. We handed on the work, and that is the best thing an order can do.
It stood on the marsh road, a little house of reed and brick with a lamp in every window. Seven sisters, and me. I was away on pilgrimage when the Hollow came.
Five days I was gone, praying for the road, and while I prayed the shrine burned. I came back to ash. I tell myself I couldn't have saved them. Some mornings I even believe it.
character.guildmark.ysolde.leave: I'm sorry, friend. Truly. I cannot walk this road with you any longer. I've prayed on it, and the light says no. May it keep you better than I could.
character.guildmark.ysolde.cold: Not yet. Let me pray on it a while longer. I'm sorry.
character.guildmark.ysolde.return: I prayed on it, and the light said you were worth one more try. Please don't make me regret it.
Light be thanked. That was bravely done.
Good work, friend. The roads are lighter for it.
A prayer well said. I felt it. Thank you.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.disappro: That wasn't yours to take, friend. Please give it back.
You killed an innocent. I can't pretend I didn't see it.
The Hearthsworn! They keep the fires now. I couldn't be happier.
The Quiet Hand? Oh, friend, no. Theft is theft, however polite.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.ask: A moment, friend, when you can? I've something to ask.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.camp.0: In my first month as a novice, I dropped the evening candle into the lamp oil. We didn't lose the shrine, but I did lose my eyebrows. Sister Edda said it suited me. She was a terrible liar and a wonderful woman.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.camp.1: I came to the Lamplighters at fourteen, after the marsh fever took my mother. The sisters gave me a lamp to carry, and told me nobody need fear the dark so long as someone kept a light. I believed them. I still do.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.camp.2: I light seven candles each night, one for every sister. It doesn't help, but it doesn't hurt either. Some nights I count them twice, in case I've missed one. I never have.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.region: A new land. I wonder whose fire we'll find in it.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.capital: So many lamps! Whoever lights these every night must be exhausted.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.night: Dusk, friend. Let's find a fire before the dark finds us.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.rain: Rain on my sandals again. Well, the road is getting washed.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.deep: I don't like it down here. So much dark, and no sky.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.hurt: You're hurt! Stand still and let me pray. Please.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.boss: That one means harm. Stay close, and let me ward you.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.victory: It's over. Light be thanked. Is everyone whole?
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.downed: Oh. Oh, that hurt. Give me a moment, friend.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.revived: Thank you. I'm up. Light keep you for that.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.respawn: You're back! Light be thanked. I was halfway through the burial prayer.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.idle.0: I like roads. Everyone who walked one wanted to get somewhere.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.idle.1: I keep thinking the sisters would have liked you. Edda especially.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.idle.2: Three candle ends and one good prayer. That will do for today.
character.guildmark.ysolde.bark.swap: Someone else walks with you? Then I'll wait here, with a candle.
character.guildmark.kestrel.meet: Heard you clear lairs. I like that in a stranger. Room at your fire?
character.guildmark.kestrel.intro: Kestrel Vey, ranger of the Thornwood, which is what poachers call themselves once they've got a decent bow. I grew up shooting what the lords said wasn't mine to shoot, and I'm better at it than their foresters ever were. You look like you're headed somewhere with teeth in it. Take me along and nothing sneaks up on you. Probably.
character.guildmark.kestrel.join: Deal. Try to keep up. I'll try to wait.
character.guildmark.kestrel.decline: Your loss. I'll be around. Waiting is most of hunting.
character.guildmark.kestrel.hello.0: Yes? You've got a look. Either you've seen something to shoot, or you want to talk. I'll take either.
character.guildmark.kestrel.hello.1: Go on, then. Make it quick. I'm counting something.
character.guildmark.kestrel.follow: Lead on. I'll be wherever the cover is.
character.guildmark.kestrel.wait: Wait here? Fine. I'll be up a tree. Wave if you need me.
character.guildmark.kestrel.part: Suit yourself. I'll hang about here a while. Find me if you want someone who can shoot.
character.guildmark.kestrel.rejoin: Missed me, did you? Thought so. Let's go.
character.guildmark.kestrel.step0: There's a spider den in the Thornwood, eating the deer out of the woods. That's my forest, whatever the lords say. Help me clear it. I'll even let you take the first shot. After mine.
character.guildmark.kestrel.step0.note: Kestrel wants the spider den that is eating the deer out of the Thornwood cleared.
character.guildmark.kestrel.step1: The Dusk Rider ran down my brother Wil on the north road, years ago, and I've waited all that time for a proper hunt. Be out in the open at dusk and it will come for us. Let's see how it likes being hunted.
character.guildmark.kestrel.step1.note: Kestrel wants the Dusk Rider brought down. It comes for you at dusk, out on the open road.
character.guildmark.kestrel.step2: There's one hunt left that anyone tells stories about. A dragon. I've dreamed of one since I could hold a bow, and I won't lie, we might not both walk off that mountain. But the story would be good.
character.guildmark.kestrel.step2.note: Kestrel wants a dragon killed. Every hunter dreams of one.
character.guildmark.kestrel.waiting: Not done yet? Don't sulk. I've waited three days for a deer. I can wait for you.
character.guildmark.kestrel.step0.done: The den's clear, and the deer will come back. Thank you. I mean that, which I don't say often, so don't make a face. I'd have managed alone. It would have been duller.
character.guildmark.kestrel.step1.done: It's down. The Dusk Rider is down. That's for you, Wil. Give me a moment, and don't say anything kind, or I'll lose it.
character.guildmark.kestrel.gated: Not yet. Ask me again when we've hunted a bit longer together.
character.guildmark.kestrel.finale: A dragon, and I'm alive to brag about it. Here. I made this from Thornwood yew, and the horn at the tip is from the hart my father was hanged for. I've never let anyone else hold it. Keep it, you've earned it, and I'm yours for as long as there's anything left to hunt.
character.guildmark.kestrel.done: Back for more? Good. Point me at something with teeth.
character.guildmark.kestrel.standing.0: Barely. I don't trust anyone I haven't seen in a real fight. Give me one.
character.guildmark.kestrel.standing.1: Wary. You haven't put a foot wrong yet. That's what bothers me. Nobody's that clean.
character.guildmark.kestrel.standing.2: Warming up. Not warm, mind. Warming. Give me a few more kills.
character.guildmark.kestrel.standing.3: Good. Better than good. You stand where I'd stand, and I notice things like that.
character.guildmark.kestrel.standing.4: Close. Closer than I'm comfortable with, if I'm honest, which I'm trying not to be. One more hunt, maybe two.
character.guildmark.kestrel.standing.5: Sworn. Which is a fancy way of saying you're stuck with me. I'm told it's an honour. I'm told a lot of things.
character.guildmark.kestrel.gift: For me? Huh. You were listening. Thanks.
character.guildmark.kestrel.gift_again: One's plenty. I don't want to get used to presents. Thanks, though.
character.guildmark.kestrel.topic.thornw: Old forest, black yew and bramble so thick a lord's horse can't ride it. Deer, boar, wolves, and anyone the law's stopped bothering to look for. I know every game trail like I know my own name.
Don't go thinking it's pretty. It's cold and it bites. But it's honest. Nothing in the Thornwood pretends to be something else, and I can't say that about anywhere with a wall round it.
character.guildmark.kestrel.topic.rider: What do you know about the Dusk Rider?
My brother Wil was walking home along the north road at dusk, with two rabbits and a fiddle. He was the only one of us who could carry a tune. It rode him down. They found the rabbits. They never found the fiddle.
Everyone says it's a ghost. A ghost doesn't leave hoofprints, and I've found them. It's a thing with a hide, and things with hides can be shot.
character.guildmark.kestrel.leave: That's it. I'm done being hauled around by someone I can't respect. Don't follow me.
character.guildmark.kestrel.cold: Don't. I'm not ready to talk. Give it a day, and a better apology.
character.guildmark.kestrel.return: Fine. I got bored without you. Just bored. Don't read anything into it.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.approve: Ha! Now that's a kill worth counting.
A contract done and paid. Good work. I'll allow it.
New country! Now we're getting somewhere.
Smooth. The rich can spare it.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.disappr: That was a commoner. We don't hunt folk like that. Ever.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.faction: Knights. You joined the knights. I'm trying not to say anything.
The Quiet Hand! Now you're interesting.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.ask: Got a moment? I want to ask you something.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.camp.0: I once sold a lord his own stag. Shot it on his land at dawn, hauled it to his kitchen door by noon, and his steward paid me full price. I still laugh whenever I see that coat of arms.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.camp.1: We lived at the edge of the Thornwood, my father, Wil and me. Father took one deer a season, no more, and only when we were short. The year the lord's foresters were watching, they hanged him from the old oak at the bend. For a deer.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.camp.2: Wil played the fiddle badly and cheerfully, loud enough to scare every deer within a mile, which drove Father mad. I'd give every kill I've ever counted to hear it ruin a hunt again.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.region: New country. Let's see what's hiding in it.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.capital: Walls, walls, walls. Wake me when we're back under open sky.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.night: Night's here. Good light for hunting, bad light for being hunted.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.rain: Rain. Wonderful. Now everything smells of wet dog, and so do I.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.deep: I don't like it down here. No sky. No sky at all.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.hurt: You're bleeding! Get back, I'll cover you. Go on!
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.boss: Big one. I'm taking the first shot. Don't argue.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.victory: That's another for the tally. I'm still ahead, by the way.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.downed: Down... I'm only down. Give me a second.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.revived: Thanks. Tell anyone and I'll deny it.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.respawn: Don't do that again. I mean it. I really mean it.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.idle.0: I'm up on you by nine kills. Just so you know.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.idle.1: Smell that? Woodsmoke and wet leaves. Best smell there is.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.idle.2: I used to hate company. Don't let that go to your head.
character.guildmark.kestrel.bark.swap: Replacing me already? Fine. I'll be in a tree.
character.guildmark.lucan.meet: Hello, sorry. I heard you know sorcery. May I sit? I talk when nervous.
character.guildmark.lucan.intro: Lucan Dray, formerly of the Starwatch, formerly the best apprentice in my year. I studied under Silvan Marrow, which is the sort of detail that ruins a reference. I talk a great deal, and I'm quite useful, in that order. Might I walk with you?
character.guildmark.lucan.join: Really? Oh, brilliant. Right. Yes. Let's go, before you change your mind.
character.guildmark.lucan.decline: Oh. Of course. Entirely fine. I'll just sit here and reorganise my notes. Again.
character.guildmark.lucan.hello.0: Yes? Sorry, was I muttering? I was in the middle of a thought about starlight. It can wait.
character.guildmark.lucan.hello.1: Hello! Don't mind me, I was only arguing with myself. I'm winning.
character.guildmark.lucan.follow: Right, yes, following. I shall be very quiet. I shan't, but I shall try.
character.guildmark.lucan.wait: Wait here, yes, fine. I'll go over my notes. I'm always going over my notes.
character.guildmark.lucan.part: I see. Well. That's fine. I'll wait here, possibly muttering. Come and find me if you need me.
character.guildmark.lucan.rejoin: Oh! You came back. Brilliant, I was running out of things to alphabetise.
character.guildmark.lucan.step0: I need ink, and not the kind from a shop. The only ink that holds a star chart is made from the dust of endermen, and I need three of them. I know, they teleport, and you mustn't look them in the eyes. That's rather why I need you.
character.guildmark.lucan.step0.note: Lucan needs the dust of three endermen, the only ink that holds a star chart.
character.guildmark.lucan.step1: I've found where the coven keeps my notebook, in a witch's hollow out in the wilds. Years of work on the weave, every margin mine, and I hear they've been writing in them. I shall never forgive that. Help me clear the hollow and take it back?
character.guildmark.lucan.step1.note: Lucan wants a witch's hollow cleared. The coven keeps his notebook there.
character.guildmark.lucan.step2: Corvin Ashe sold my notebook, and now he's taken an old Starwatch archive for himself and filled it with fangs and spirits. He was my friend. I want to ask him why, which is a polite way of saying I want to hit him with a staff. Will you come with me?
character.guildmark.lucan.step2.note: Lucan wants the Ashe Archive cleared, and Corvin Ashe with it.
character.guildmark.lucan.waiting: Still out there? Yes, yes, take your time. I'll be here, worrying quietly.
character.guildmark.lucan.step0.done: Three! And the dust! Oh, look at the colour, it's practically singing. Thank you. I'll have the first chart inked by morning, and I will not stop talking about it.
character.guildmark.lucan.step1.done: My notebook. My actual notebook, and they have been writing in the margins! I'll forgive that, just this once, because you got it back. Thank you. I would have been a coward on my own.
character.guildmark.lucan.gated: Not yet. Ask me again when, well, when I know you better. Sorry.
character.guildmark.lucan.finale: It's done. I thought I'd feel something dramatic, and mostly I feel tired. Here, I want you to have this. I made it as an apprentice and wound the haft with a strip of my old robe, and I've sewn the silver star back on at the head, the one I unpicked. It's the only part of the Starwatch I wanted to keep, and now it's yours, and so am I.
character.guildmark.lucan.done: Ah, there you are. I've had three new ideas and I'm going to tell you all of them.
character.guildmark.lucan.standing.0: Cold, I should think. You barely know me, I barely know you, and I've been nervously talking at you for days. I'm sorry about that.
character.guildmark.lucan.standing.1: Wary. Both of us. I'm trying not to say something stupid. I haven't managed it yet, but I'm trying.
character.guildmark.lucan.standing.2: Warming, I think? I hope? I'm bad at reading these things. Books are easier.
character.guildmark.lucan.standing.3: Trusting. I'd trust you with my notebook, and I hope you know what that means.
character.guildmark.lucan.standing.4: Nearly sworn. I'd say I'm honoured, but honestly I'm terrified. In a good way.
character.guildmark.lucan.standing.5: Sworn. I never thought anyone would have me again. I'm still not entirely sure you're real. I mean that kindly.
character.guildmark.lucan.gift: A gift? For me? Oh, I do like it. Thank you. That's exactly right.
character.guildmark.lucan.gift_again: Another? No, no, you mustn't, you've been so kind today already. Tomorrow! I shall look forward to it.
character.guildmark.lucan.topic.starwatc: Wonderful. Towers in the capitals, a library the size of a village, and four hundred years of watching the sky and writing it all down. I'd have given my right hand to be a Star one day. Though I'd have needed it for casting.
They put me out the week Silvan turned. No hearing, no trial. It was for the good of the order, and I understand that. I hate that I understand.
character.guildmark.lucan.topic.marrow.0: He was the best teacher I ever had, and the kindest, to me. He'd stay up past midnight over a single line of a ward until I understood it. He used to say sorcery was the only honest craft.
character.guildmark.lucan.topic.marrow.1: I keep going over the last year, looking for the moment it turned. I was there for all of it, and I never noticed. How is that possible? I'm supposed to be clever.
character.guildmark.lucan.leave: I can't do this. I've been put out of one place already, and I won't stay where I'm not wanted. Goodbye.
character.guildmark.lucan.cold: No. Not yet. Please don't ask. I'm still writing my side of the argument.
character.guildmark.lucan.return: I thought it over. At rather exhausting length, you'll be unsurprised to hear. You're worth another try. Don't make me regret it.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.approve.f: Brilliant! That was magnificent. I'm taking notes.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.approve.m: Oh, nicely cast! Textbook. Better than textbook, actually.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.approve.l: A new land! There's so much to study here.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.disapprov: You can't just take that. Well, you can. You shouldn't.
Oh no. No. That was a person. A real person.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.faction.s: You joined the Starwatch. That's lovely. I'm perfectly fine.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.faction.q: The Quiet Hand? Thieves. I'm not saying don't. I'm saying don't.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.starwatch: Silvan is stopped. I'm glad, and I'm grieving. Thank you for both.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.ask: When you've a moment, I'd like a word. Not urgent. Slightly urgent.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.camp.0: I once set fire to the Starwatch's reading room. A small fire. An educational fire. The Magister said nothing for a week, which is the worst thing he can say.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.camp.1: I was nine when the Starwatch took me. A woman held up a crystal in our village, and it hummed when I looked at it. My mother cried, and I thought she was sad. It was years before I understood she was proud.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.camp.2: Silvan taught me the weave by hand, line by line, and read me his notes at midnight. Near the end he stopped reading them to me. I told myself he was busy. I'm the cleverest person I know, and I told myself he was busy.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.region: A new land! There'll be a hundred things to write down.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.capital: Lovely capital. The Starwatch has a tower here. Let's not look up.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.night: Look up! That's why the Starwatch watches. Isn't it beautiful?
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.rain: Rain. Typical. There goes the sky for the evening.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.deep: Underground. The rock is very old, I'm told. I'd prefer it elsewhere.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.hurt: You're hurt! Fall back, fall back, I've got you!
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.boss: That's a boss. That's definitely a boss. I haven't read about that.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.victory: We won! I mean, obviously. I had faith. A little. Some.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.downed: Ow. Ow ow. Down. Quite down. Just a moment.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.revived: Thank you. Terribly sorry. I did say I was fragile.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.respawn: You're alive! I thought, that is, I was fairly sure. Welcome back!
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.idle.0: I've been thinking about the nature of light. I'll spare you. Mostly.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.idle.1: I can almost hear the stars. A lie, but a good one.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.idle.2: I wonder if anyone's reading my notebook right now. Don't answer that.
character.guildmark.lucan.bark.swap: Oh. Someone else. Of course. I'll wait here, alphabetising.

handbook.guildmark.page15:
ERRANDS

A guild leader can send sworn members away on errands with /guild. They come back richer and tougher.

Mostly.

Sneak + click: heavy. Hold to charge it.

handbook.guildmark.page17:
READING A FOE

Every swing, roll and guard costs stamina.

Watch the wind-up, not the blade. Break a foe's poise and it reels, open to a riposte.

And mind the old soldiers on the roads at night.

Some stories are bigger than a notice board.

- The Guild Clerk

lore.guildmark.30.title: Lore: The Unbowed
lore.guildmark.30.page0: When the Hollow King rose, every power in the land was called to kneel. The dragons of the high peaks alone did not, and fire was all they ever answered him with.
lore.guildmark.30.page1: They are called the Unbowed. Each keeps a hoard on a summit, sleeps on it by night and circles it by day, and suffers no one on its mountain.
lore.guildmark.31.title: Lore: The Grasp of the Deep
lore.guildmark.31.page0: Sailors say the sea has a floor, and under it another sea, where the Maelgrasp sleeps. When a ship strays over the deeps by night it wakes: the wind dies, and her bell rings with no hand on it.
lore.guildmark.31.page1: Then it takes hold. Arms like masts rise round her, and one great eye watches from the water. Its beak, lashed to a stem, keeps the lesser hunters off: they know what wore it.
